The clinical presentation is highly characteristic of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM): exertional syncope in a young, otherwise healthy individual; physical exam findings of prominent jugular A waves (indicating forceful atrial contraction against a stiff, noncompliant left ventricle) and an S4 gallop (reflecting impaired ventricular compliance); ECG showing LVH voltage criteria; and imaging (echo and CMR) confirming asymmetric septal hypertrophy with small LV cavity — the hallmark morphologic features of HCM. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
